transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been seeing and hearing things at work and at home that no one else seems to notice, and it’s starting to scare me. I don't really know how to explain it, but it feels like I'm losing my grip on what's real.
How long have you been experiencing these sights and sounds?

I've been dealing with the whispers and those shadowy figures pretty steadily for about the past ten months. It started a few months after all the changes at my job, and it just hasn't really stopped since then. It's honestly terrifying because it feels so constant and real.
Along with these experiences, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or lost interest in your usual activities during these past ten months?

Yes, outside of my high-energy spells, I feel completely flat, blank, and drained. I've lost all interest in things I used to love, like my art group and hiking, and I just skip them because I can't bring myself to care enough to get up and go. It's like I have no motivation left on those days.
You mentioned having high-energy spells and low-energy periods. Do you ever experience the whispers or shadowy figures during times when your mood feels completely normal and stable?

Yes, earlier this year there was a stretch of a few weeks where my mood felt completely neutral, with no big highs or crashes. Even though I wasn't buzzing with energy or big ideas, I was still hearing my name whispered and felt convinced the company emails were coded messages about me. It was scary because those experiences stayed even when my mood felt stable.
Looking back over the last ten months, would you say these high-energy spells and low-energy periods have been present for most of that time, or did they only happen occasionally?

Yes, they've been present for the vast majority of the time. I've spent most of this past year in those revved-up, high-energy phases, barely sleeping and chasing big ideas with only brief breaks. Those amped-up periods have definitely dominated over the flatter, low-energy times.
During those high-energy spells, how long do they typically last without stopping, and do you experience other symptoms like racing thoughts or speaking much faster than usual?

These amped-up phases have been going on for almost the entire past year with only brief breaks, and my mind absolutely races with ideas I feel I have to act on right away. When I start talking about them, I speak so fast and jump from one thought to the next that people get confused or cut me off because of the intense pressure I feel to explain it all.

During these high-energy periods, have your racing thoughts and behaviors ever caused significant problems in your life, like major financial trouble, risky actions, or even needing to be hospitalized?

I haven't been hospitalized or gone bankrupt, but these periods have severely disrupted my life. I've missed major deadlines and had projects taken away at work, and my wife has had to take over managing our bills and appointments because I can't keep track of anything. It ultimately got so bad that HR had to contact her, which is what brought me to this evaluation.
During those high-energy phases, how would you describe your mood—did you feel unusually happy, euphoric, or extremely irritable, or was it mostly just a physical feeling of having a lot of energy?

I'll go from feeling on top of the world and weirdly giddy—like I’m the only one who really understands how everything connects—to being extremely irritable. During those times, I'll snap at my wife and coworkers over tiny things, slam doors, or fire off sharp emails because I suddenly feel like everyone is against me or wasting my time. It's a constant swing between those two extremes.
During those high-energy phases when you are barely sleeping, do you still feel fully rested and energized despite getting only a few hours of sleep?

Yes, I can easily go two or three nights sleeping only a couple of hours, sometimes just dozing in my chair, and still wake up feeling completely charged. I feel like I don't even need sleep because my mind is racing with so many ideas that I feel I have to act on right away.

opening_question.question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a 10-month history of concurrent psychotic and mood symptoms, meeting the criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder (F25). The patient experienced prominent manic episodes (euphoria/irritability, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, pressured speech, and goal-directed activity) and depressive periods (anhedonia, flat affect, lack of motivation) that were present for the majority of the illness. Crucially, the patient also experienced persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory and visual hallucinations, delusions of reference) during a period of at least a few weeks when their mood was completely stable and neutral, satisfying the requirement that psychotic symptoms must persist in the absence of prominent mood symptoms.
